record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: Let alpha be an algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have modulus greater than one, let N(alpha) be the absolute norm of alpha over Q, and set B = {0, ±1, ±2, ..., ±(N(alpha)-1)}. Is there a simple proof that Z[alpha] equals B[alpha]?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Let α be an algebraic integer whose all conjugates are greater than one in modulus and N(α) be the absolute norm of α over Q. Set B = {0, ±1, ±2, . . . , ±(N(α) − 1)}. Is there an easy proof of Z[α] = B[α] ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha$ be an algebraic integer such that every Galois conjugate of $\alpha$ (over $\mathbb{Q}$), including $\alpha$ itself, has absolute value strictly greater than $1$. Let
$$N(\alpha) = \left|\mathrm{N}_{\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)/\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\right|$$
denote the absolute value of the field norm of $\alpha$, and set
$$B = \{0, \pm 1, \pm 2, \ldots, \pm(N(\alpha)-1)\} \subset \mathbb{Z}.$$
Define $B[\alpha]$ to be the set of all finite sums $\sum_{i=0}^{n} b_i \alpha^i$ with $n \ge 0$ and $b_i \in B$.

Provide a simple/elementary proof (or show that no such proof exists) of the equality
$$\mathbb{Z}[\alpha] = B[\alpha].$$
That is, show that every element of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ can be written as a polynomial in $\alpha$ with integer coefficients drawn from $B$.
artifact.status_search_result: The equality $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]=B[\alpha]$ is known to hold (it follows from results in the theory of beta-expansions and canonical/digit number systems for expanding algebraic integers), but the question explicitly asks for a *simple/easy* proof. No elementary self-contained proof appears in the literature found; the problem is posed as an open challenge for finding such a proof, and recent works on digit expansions in algebraic bases continue to rely on nontrivial machinery.

status_evidence.title: Digit expansions in rational and algebraic basis
status_evidence.snippet: α-expansions generalize rational base number systems and expand elements in base α with digits in a specific digit set, related to canonical number systems and rational self-affine tiles.
status_evidence.claim: Recent treatments of digit expansions for algebraic bases use nontrivial tile-theoretic and canonical-number-system machinery rather than an elementary argument.

status_evidence.title: On β-adic expansions of powers of an algebraic integer omitting a digit
status_evidence.snippet: Studies β-adic expansions where β is an expanding algebraic integer, building on the standard digit set {0,1,...,|N(β)|-1}.
status_evidence.claim: The standard digit set used for expanding algebraic integers is the one of cardinality |N(β)|, consistent with the problem's setup, but representability proofs rely on dynamical/tile arguments.
